page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors running on the x86_64 architecture. The server delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores with two threads per core and a base clock speed of 3.5 GHz. It includes 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding an even 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware-level acceleration includes AVX-512 with VNNI, alongside hardware cryptography instructions including AES and SHA-NI. The configuration includes 7,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 200 Gbps network interface, but contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight superior multi-threaded compute density and high uncached throughput. The server scores within the top 10% on PassMark CPU benchmarks (87,437.78), extended instruction sets, and CPU encryption tests. It also achieves top-tier results in Geekbench ray tracing and image processing, supported by strong Geekbench multi-core scores and clang compilation speed. While single-thread benchmarks such as single-core Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the middle 50% tier, multi-core stress-ng registers in the top 25% with 125,012.51. In-memory data structures perform strongly, as shown by Redis SET throughput reaching 110.23 million operations per second and high uncached read memory bandwidth of 339.12 GB/sec.

The bare-metal setup eliminates virtualization overhead, offering high resource density across compute, memory, and fast local NVMe storage. Qualitative trade-offs emerge between single-threaded execution and parallel throughput; workloads relying strictly on per-core clock speed see moderate performance, while highly parallel tasks scale efficiently. Because it lacks dedicated GPU hardware, text generation on large language models drops off significantly, recording weak metrics on 70B parameter models. Consequently, m6idn.metal is best matched for high-throughput databases, static web serving clusters, large-scale CI/CD compilation, and enterprise analytics that leverage local NVMe storage and multi-threaded CPU parallelization.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs (64 physical cores) powered by 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processors on x86_64 architecture. The server supplies 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 7,600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and 200 Gbps baseline networking, operating without dedicated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded processing, leading PassMark CPU scores, and strong Redis operation rates of 110.23 million operations per second. While single-core metrics fall within average boundaries and larger LLM generation is limited by the absence of GPU acceleration, its substantial memory bandwidth and raw physical core count offer high resource efficiency for parallel workloads. The server is well positioned for enterprise relational databases, large-scale software compilation, in-memory caches, and high-throughput web serving.
